question: What supported Linux companion boundary should follow the landed local-Gateway shell: remote operator support only, remote operator plus separately opt-in node mode, or no further first-party parity work yet?
rationale: The next increment determines credential handoff, privileged IPC isolation, local service behavior, node capability exposure, packaging ownership, and which core CLI contract the desktop may consume; source inspection cannot choose those product and security boundaries safely.

options.title: Remote operator plus opt-in node
options.body: Keep Control UI connectivity and laptop-node registration independent, add a canonical validated remote target/auth contract, and require two-machine security and failure-state proof.

options.title: Remote operator only
options.body: Add direct or Tailscale remote-Gateway operation while deferring all Linux node capabilities and pairing UI to a later decision.

options.title: Pause at local MVP
options.body: Treat the current local-Gateway shell as the supported Linux scope and close or split remaining parity requests until app work becomes a higher priority.

recommendation.title: Remote operator plus opt-in node
recommendation.body: Keep Control UI connectivity and laptop-node registration independent, add a canonical validated remote target/auth contract, and require two-machine security and failure-state proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue history shows the clearest product-priority and native-platform direction from this contributor, with security and core priorities explicitly framing app work.
